title: You’ll Barely Feel These Lightweight Sunscreens on Your Skin - Allure

 They glide on like silk, dry down with no cast or residue, and keep your skin safe. By Kara Nesvig November 16, 2026 Collage: Jemeria Davison; Source images: Courtesy of brands and editors Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story We’re obsessed with sunscreen here at Allure , but the best lightweight sunscreens are in a league of their own. You know (or already should know) that SPF is the most important step in any skin-care routine to protect your gorgeous visage from the damaging effects of the sun and fend off signs of aging, but everyone has their preferences when it comes to formulas— chemical , mineral , hybrid, tinted or not, etc. Yes, lightweight sunscreens layer well without any stickiness or that lingering feeling that something is sitting underneath your makeup or on your bare skin; what else is so great about them?
 “Lightweight sunscreens are particularly appealing to people with acne-prone or oily skin who dislike the heavy or greasy feel of traditional sunscreens,” explains Jenna Queller , MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in Boca Raton, Florida. However, they’re not just for oily skin types. Dr. Queller says they’re a good pick for people who live in hot, humid climates (like her patients in sunny Florida) or anyone who likes layering sunscreen with makeup or other skin care.

 Ultimately, any derm or editor will tell you what matters most is finding a formula you like and will faithfully wear daily, and to get you started, we rounded up some of the most elegant, lightweight sunscreens on the market. While there’s no such thing as completely invisible sunscreen (yet), these lightweight formulas are the next best thing.
 Best Mineral Overall: La Roche-Posay UVAir Mineral SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen
 Save to wishlist Save to wishlist La Roche-Posay
 UVAir Mineral SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen
 $40 Amazon
 $43 La Roche-Posay
 Allure senior commerce director Shanna Shipin applying the La Roche-Posay UVAir Mineral SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen
 Shanna Shipin Why it’s worth it: Even the name “UVAir” implies that it’s lightweight. The UVAir Mineral SPF Serum Sunscreen from derm-beloved La Roche-Posay glides onto skin and leaves almost no trace behind, beautifully living up to its moniker. UVAir wins our best mineral title because it couldn’t be easier to incorporate into your skin-care routine, especially if you’re reluctant to pile too much on your face or you hate feeling like you have “stuff” sitting on your skin.
 In addition to its sun-blocking benefits, niacinamide helps fade dark spots over time, and hyaluronic acid and glycerin intensely hydrate without heaviness. The mineral formula leaves no white cast behind, just potent protection. If you’ve got a sunscreen-hater in your life or are looking for the lightest possible formula around, UVAir is a safe bet.
 Shipin before applying the La Roche-Posay UVAir Mineral SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen
 Shanna Shipin Shipin after applying the La Roche-Posay UVAir Mineral SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen
 Shanna Shipin Tester feedback from senior commerce director Shanna Shipin 
 AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron "I've heard many derms say, "The best sunscreen is the one you'll use every day," which makes UV Air the best for me! I have almost no qualms with this product—and that's saying a lot as someone who hasn't had quite a Goldilocks experience with mineral formulations. They're often thick, grainy, and leave a white cast. Not so with UV Air Mineral; as the name suggests, it's light as you-know-what, feels more like a serum than a sunscreen, and it instantly melts into the skin, disappearing in less than 5 seconds. This is one of the reasons I use it more than any other mineral sunscreen; typically, you have to rub the formula in for at least 30 seconds for it to dissipate. As someone who's chronically late and has two kids, I really value beauty products that I don't need to wait on.
 The formula is very much like a serum, and that's the only slight negative; it's quite runny, so if you're not careful, you may drip some onto your clothes (or, in my case, the car, where I'm often reapplying). That said, it's far more stable than other formulas I've tried, so it's a small gripe (I hardly even have to shake it up before applying—another win!). The sunscreen is virtually undetectable on my medium skin tone, and I've never had any issues layering my typical makeup over top. It's also an adorable package; the sunscreen is stout, easy to squeeze out, and has a large top that feels intentional and sturdy when you close it. I keep mine in my daily bag, and it's never exploded." —Shanna Shipin, senior commerce director

 Why it’s worth it: Yes, the Supergoop Unseen Sunscreen SPF 50 applies as effortlessly as your favorite silk slip dress—and yes, it feels like you’re wearing nothing at all. So why wouldn’t you want to wear this sunscreen every day? A Best of Beauty and Readers' Choice Award winner breezes through the checklist of sunscreen must-haves: unscented, never sticky, with zero chance of a white cast or pilling. As a bonus, it does double duty as a blurring makeup primer and helps visibly even skin thanks to licorice root and chamomile-derived bisabolol, an ingredient known for its soothing properties. Even sensitive skin types can use it without irritation, but make sure you’re applying enough, as it’s so sheer you might miss a spot if you’re not careful!

After applying it, my roommate literally looked at me and said, “Wait, you have sunscreen on? I couldn’t even tell.” The application is incredibly smooth. I used to find applying sunscreen a bit of a hassle, but this formula glides onto the skin effortlessly. I’m also someone who hates the feeling of heavy products on my face (unless we’re talking about a thick, moisturizing formula during the winter months). It’s one of the reasons I rarely wear foundation. Luckily, this sunscreen feels lightweight, almost as if I’m not wearing anything at all. I also enjoy the subtle sunscreen scent. It has that familiar smell without being overpowering or suffocating. My only real downside is the price. However, considering sunscreen is something you should be applying every day, I think it’s worth investing in a formula you actually enjoy using.” —Hailey Roy, commerce editorial assistant

Even though it’s blissfully lightweight and goes on actually clear, not white like a traditional sunscreen, I always feel protected—which is why it’ll be coming along with me on my upcoming trip to Palm Springs!  Allure commerce editor Madison San Miguel applying the Colorscience Sunforgettable Total Protection Face Shield Flex SPF 50 PA++++
 Madison San Miguel Why it’s worth it: Low-maintenance folks, meet your new sunscreen BFF. This tinted formula knocks out a few steps of your daily routine, blurring any imperfections and adding just a teeny bit of color to sub in for other complexion makeup. Colorescience’s Sunforgettable Total Protection Face Shield comes in six shades, spanning from Fair to Rich Deep, creating customizable coverage with a demi-matte finish. Though the formula starts as a white cream, the “Flex” refers to the encapsulated iron oxide pigments, which adapt to suit your skin tone as they’re rubbed in. (These iron oxides also help protect against blue light , which can also lead to signs of early skin aging.)
 Skin-care ingredients like antioxidants—including silver ear mushroom and a complex called Lipochroman—reduce free radical damage and help fight skin aging from the pollutants we encounter in our daily lives. If you’re curious about the PA++++, it's a Japanese-based rating system defined by + to ++++ to show how well a product can block UVA rays.

I use it as my ‘foundation’ regardless of the type of makeup look I do, and it provides just enough coverage to conceal post-acne marks and redness without feeling greasy or heavy. I once had a nurse ask me what I was wearing post-microneedling sesh, and she was stunned by its coverage!” —Madison San Miguel, commerce editor

 Best Brightening: Mediheal Madecassoside Moisture Sun Serum SPF 50+
 Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Mediheal
 Madecassoside Moisture Sun Serum SPF 50+
 $22 Amazon
 $22 Ulta Beauty
 Why it’s worth it: Because South Korea—like much of the world—works with more advanced SPF filters that aren’t yet approved by the FDA here, we’re missing some seriously good K-beauty sunscreens. But Korean brands are trying their best to provide just-as-elegant formulas to rival the originals—like this milky, serum-inspired formula. Mediheal’s Madecassoside Moisture Sun Serum SPF 50+ is unique for a few reasons, the first being its watery, lightweight texture, which feels delightfully refreshing upon application. The formula is centered around the botanical extract Centella asiatica , which is also known as cica. First is the derivative called madecassoside, which soothes, hydrates, and provides antioxidant protection.
 Four types of cica make up a complex called 4-TECA, a.k.a. a powerhouse combo of madecassoside, madecassic acid, asiaticoside, and asiatic acid to refresh and calm skin. Niacinamide, a vitamin B derivative, helps evens skin tone and makes skin look more radiant overall. After wearing it for a few days, you’ll see why we can’t stop clamoring for more K-beauty formulas to make their way stateside.

While that means I can't compare the Korean and US versions, I can vouch for how good the latter is! K-beauty has really nailed the concept of serum sunscreens—my all-time favorite is actually called a sun ampoule—which are just as lightweight as they sound. Like serums, these formulas are definitely on the fluid side, which is why they absorb oh so quickly into your skin and feel like nothing from the moment they touch your skin. This one in particular is incredibly calming: It doesn't just have cica, but *six* types of the super-soother, and niacinamide helps brighten my morning dullness. The nozzle is also very slim, which helps the liquidy formula dispense more precisely onto my fingers without running everywhere. (However, I'd suggest not dawdling during application!) Overall, I highly recommend the Madecassoside Moisture Sun Serum to anyone who's ever complained about how heavy sunscreens feel—so, basically everyone?” —Sarah Han, commerce editor

 Frequently Asked Questions 
 What makes a sunscreen lightweight? 
 Key components of a lightweight sunscreen include a formula that “spreads easily, absorbs comfortably, and leaves the skin feeling neither greasy nor heavy,” explains Dr. Queller. “Some sunscreens have a more fluid texture and a less noticeable finish, making them easier to wear every day, especially under makeup .”
 Dr. Queller says that chemical sunscreens tend to be the lighter of the two, as the zinc and titanium dioxide in mineral formulas may feel heavier on the skin and have been known to leave a white cast; however, the mineral sunscreens of today have an improved texture and finish to compete with their chemical counterparts.
 Whatever your texture preference, Dr. Queller puts it best: “The sunscreen you’ll actually apply consistently is the one that will best protect your skin over time,” so find a broad-spectrum sunscreen that feels good to wear and stick with it. 
 What are serum sunscreens, and how are they formulated? 
 With roots in K-beauty , serum sunscreens are becoming more popular as consumers continue exploring different sunscreen formats. They’re exactly what they sound like: more fluid formulas designed to glide on and feel extremely lightweight on skin. As Dr. Queller notes, some formulas also contain skin-care ingredients like niacinamide or hyaluronic acid to give you more bang for your sun-protection buck. “But don’t let the serum texture fool you into applying less,” she says. “You still need adequate sun protection, which means applying generously to the face, ears, neck, and chest.” (As a general guideline, follow the two-finger rule for your face—and add extra for your neck and chest as needed.)
 How we test and review products 
 When Allure tests a product , our editors look at it from every angle in an effort to best serve you. We review ingredients, scrutinize brand claims, and, when necessary, examine peer-reviewed scientific and medical studies. In addition to testing each and every product that's included in each and every review, we rely on experts who shape their fields, including dermatology, cosmetic chemistry, and medicine, to help us vet the ingredients and formulas.
 For our list of the best lightweight sunscreens, we considered each product's performance across five primary categories: product ingredients and efficacy, packaging, fragrance, texture, and product wear. Every product was determined to have excelled in each category by our editorial team, which is composed of in-house writers and editors as well as contributors—along with special consideration from board-certified dermatologists. To learn more information on our reporting and testing processes, read our complete reviews process and methodology page .
 Our staff and testers 
 A beauty product is a personal purchase. You might be searching for a face cream to address persistent dryness or a new nail product to add to your Sunday self-care routine; you may simply be browsing around for the latest launches to hit the hair market. No matter what you seek or your individual needs and concerns, Allure wants to ensure that you love anything we recommend in our stories. We believe that having a diverse team of writers and editors—in addition to the wide range of outside testers and industry experts we regularly call upon—is essential to reaching that goal.
 After all, can we really say a skin-care product is the "best" for people over 50 if the only testers we’ve solicited opinions from folks who have yet to hit 30? Can we honestly deem a high-end diffuser worthy of your hard-earned cash if it’s never been tested on curls? We’re proud that our staff spans a wide range of ages, skin tones, hair textures, genders, and backgrounds, which means that we are able to fairly assess any beauty product that comes into the beauty closet.
